# Grounding & Verdict-Discipline Checklist: Mandatory "smallest version" and "what this deletes" sections; second mechanism is REWORK

**Purpose**: Validate the requirement-writing quality of this feature's core theme — citation
discipline, scope discipline, and verdict clarity — as unit tests for the English in `spec.md`.
**Created**: 2026-09-11
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: Generated by `/speckit.checklist`. Domain inferred from spec content: grounding
(principle XIII), smallest-version discipline (principle XII), and second-mechanism verdict
clarity — since `checklists/requirements.md` already covers generic spec quality.

## Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Does the spec state what happens to a claim that has no citation, for every claim type (not just Measurable Impact)? [Spec §Requirements FR-004]
- [x] CHK002 Does the spec define the full triage verdict set and its priority order, not just "redundant → rejected"? [Spec §Requirements FR-001]
- [x] CHK003 Does the spec state what a valid "nothing to delete" answer requires? [Spec §Requirements FR-003, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec state which artifact (comment, PRD section, label) carries a non-`PRD` triage verdict to the issue itself? [Gap — left to `plan.md`/stage design, not spec]

## Clarity

- [x] CHK005 Is "an already-served need" given any disambiguating criterion, or left to reviewer judgement? [Spec §User Story 2 Acceptance 1 — left to judgement by design, consistent with `cto-review`'s existing REWORK dimensions]
- [x] CHK006 Is "speculative generality" defined by example rather than only by label? [Spec §User Story 2 Acceptance 2 — "unused configuration or a one-caller abstraction"]
- [x] CHK007 Is "measured number" distinguished from an estimate or a round-number guess? [Spec §Requirements FR-004 — implicit via "cite a file:line or measured number"; no explicit estimate-vs-measurement distinction, acceptable at spec level]

## Consistency

- [x] CHK008 Does the triage verdict order in FR-001 match the order named in the Acceptance criteria of User Story 1? [Spec §Requirements FR-001 vs §User Story 1 Acceptance 1 — both: DELETE/RETIRE, CLOSE, RE-SCOPE, PRD]
- [x] CHK009 Is the REWORK verdict in User Story 2 consistent with `cto-review`'s existing verdict vocabulary (no new verdict invented)? [Spec §User Story 2 — reuses REWORK]
- [x] CHK010 Do FR-002 (issue-to-prd) and FR-005 (cto-review) use the same standard for "already-served need" so the two skills don't diverge on the same concept? [Spec §Requirements FR-002, FR-005 — both require naming the mechanism]

## Measurability

- [x] CHK011 Is SC-001 ("both new sections, non-templated") objectively checkable without interpretation? [Spec §Success Criteria SC-001]
- [x] CHK012 Is SC-003 ("no skill source... recommends anything but REWORK/retire") checkable by a repo-wide search, or does it require subjective judgement? [Spec §Success Criteria SC-003 — checkable via `grep`, confirmed in this implementation pass]
- [x] CHK013 Is SC-004 (skills-sync clean) tied to a concrete pass/fail command rather than a vague "should sync fine"? [Spec §Success Criteria SC-004]

## Coverage

- [x] CHK014 Does the spec cover both the "genuine gap → PRD" flow and the "duplicate → non-PRD" flow for User Story 1? [Spec §User Story 1 Acceptance 1-2]
- [x] CHK015 Does the spec cover both REWORK triggers (second mechanism, speculative generality) for User Story 2, or only one? [Spec §User Story 2 Acceptance 1-2]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the spec address what happens when a claim is cited but the citation is wrong/stale (not just "no citation")? [Gap — out of scope per Assumptions; citation *staleness* is not addressed, only citation *absence*]

## Edge Cases

- [x] CHK017 Is the "smallest version equals full scope" edge case resolved (section still required, not skippable)? [Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK018 Is the "in-progress migration, old mechanism not yet retired" edge case resolved for `cto-review`'s verdict? [Spec §Edge Cases — REWORK still fires unless retired in the same change]
- [x] CHK019 Is there an edge case for a triage verdict on an issue that has *already* been fully resolved elsewhere (neither a duplicate ask nor an oversized ask, just stale)?
